heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Overture TPU 95A out of the box using its direct drive extruder, provided filament is fed externally rather than through the AMS. With a maximum volumetric flow rate capped at 4.5 mm³/s, the safe calculated maximum print speed is 54 mm/s to prevent extruder buckling.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVA glue stick or liquid glue as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 4.5 mm³/s in the filament settings to automatically throttle print speeds under 54 mm/s.
Bypass the AMS and route filament directly from an external dry box to the direct drive toolhead to avoid jams.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' (Max detour length: 0) to minimize stringing and travel moves across outer perimeters.
Disable or reduce Pressure Advance to 0.02 - 0.04 to prevent excessive micro-retractions that grind flexible filament.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder Gear Jam / Filament Wrapping around Drive Gear
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing too fast or applying high backpressure, forcing flexible TPU to buckle inside the extruder cavity.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Limit Maximum Volumetric Speed strictly to 4.5 mm³/s and decrease print speed to 30-40 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption due to hygroscopic nature of TPU or excessive nozzle temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours and lower nozzle temperature to 220°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Bed Damage / Over-Adhesion on PEI Sheet
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: TPU molecularly bonds to smooth and textured PEI surfaces when printed directly without a barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue to serve as an interface release agent.

faq.question: Can I feed Overture TPU 95A through the Bambu Lab AMS on the P1S?
faq.answer: No, flexible filaments like TPU 95A will bind and tangle inside the AMS internal feeders and PTFE routing tubes; always feed from the rear spool holder or an external drybox.

faq.question: Should I keep the P1S front door or top glass open when printing TPU?
faq.answer: Yes, it is recommended to prop the top glass lid or crack the front door open to keep chamber temperatures low and prevent heat creep.

faq.question: Does Overture TPU 95A require a hardened steel nozzle upgrade on the P1S?
faq.answer: No, Overture TPU 95A is non-abrasive and can be printed safely using the stock stainless steel nozzle installed on the P1S.

faq.question: What is the recommended drying procedure for Overture TPU before printing?
faq.answer: Dry the filament in a dedicated filament dryer or the P1S heated bed at 65°C for at least 6-8 hours before printing, and print directly from a sealed dry box.
